question: How to draw every street and every building footprint in a static site with Leaflet and hand-written canvas code (the site vendors Leaflet 1.9.4 and forbids map frameworks and CDNs): measured rendering cost, per-tile JSON size model, zoom thresholds, street-name labels on canvas, USGS raster as the street source, and the field-sheet look.
scope_note: Measurements on one 4-vCPU Xeon VM with headless Chromium 141 and software raster; no GPU canvas. Device numbers are not measured.
bottom_line: Draw the streets, footprints and house dots on a few hand-written canvas layers that load by shard and cull to the view; do not give Leaflet one object per feature: each path object costs about 1.6 KB of heap here (40 MB for 25,000 paths) and Leaflet re-projects all of them on every zoom (0.3 s at 1x and 1.1 s at 2x of zoom update). The drawing itself is about as fast in Leaflet's canvas as in a raw canvas. On this 4-vCPU VM with software canvas, a redraw of the real Billings tile takes about 11 to 27 ms (measured at zooms 15 and 16; zoom 17 was not run on the real tile); the all-visible synthetic worst case (about 20,000 paths and 3,000 labels) takes 1.3 to 3 s per redraw, so the view must hold few features. Thresholds: arterials from zoom 13, local streets and house dots from 15, footprint fills from 16, names from 16 (one per name per shard, fit and collision tested, angles quantised to 5 degrees, at most 300 labels per view with the halo). Shards: cap by bytes (150 KB for streets, 250 KB for footprints) and by rows for addresses (2,500 rows, under 175 KB); the store tile is 165 KB of streets, 4.5 MB of footprints and 2.2 MB of addresses before splitting. The B3 zoom 13 address dots fetch 4.2 MB per Billings view: propose zoom 15 for dots, which is an owner decision.

draw_order: 1 basemap (the existing vector base or the USGS imagery, unchanged)
2 footprint fills with a 0.5 px hairline (from zoom 16; token --bldg-fill at 45 percent light, 60 percent dark)
3 local streets at 1.0 to 1.4 px, then arterials at 2.4 px (one canvas layer per class, batches of about 200 paths)
4 radar or model picture (existing overlay, 72 percent)
5 hazard fills at 12 percent and 2 px strokes (existing); watch and advisory strokes get a 1 px paper casing (contrast 3.2:1 and 3.3:1 over a footprint fill in light mode)
7 house dots, clickable, above the hazards (from zoom 15)
8 street names last, 12 px, name colour with a paper halo, no pointer events

label_rule.candidates: one candidate per distinct FULLNAME per shard, on the middle vertex of that name's longest piece in the shard; blank names get none
label_rule.fit_test: keep the name only if its longest piece is at least the measured label width plus 10 px at that zoom (79 percent of names at zoom 16; 93 percent at zoom 17)
label_rule.collision: greedy placement on a 64 px grid with each rotated label's bounding box; arterials first, then longer pieces; a label may not overlap another label or a house dot
label_rule.angle: quantise label angles to 5 degrees: 300 labels with halo took 7 to 13 ms quantised against 145 to 165 ms unquantised (two runs)
label_rule.cap: at most 300 labels per view while the halo is a stroke (quantised: 300 labels with halo 7 to 13 ms; 1,000 labels with halo 340 to 425 ms; 1,000 labels without halo 11 to 13 ms; the offset-fill halo was not cheaper)

recommendation.drawing: one canvas layer per class, not one Leaflet object per feature; load the shards the viewport touches; cull by shard and by feature bounds; project each vertex to world pixels once per zoom and treat pan as an offset; redraw on moveend and zoomend only, never during a drag; stroke per feature (measured; batching all features into one path was slower), never one path for all features; keep feature data in typed arrays (about 0.2 KB per feature against about 1.6 KB per path as Leaflet objects)
measure_in_build: shard bytes per layer and per cell size: raw, gzip level 6 and the size Pages serves; largest shard; shard count; statewide totals (this record gives the first numbers)
fetch count and bytes per 1280x800 and 390x844 viewport at zooms 13, 15 and 17, at several centres (Billings, Benchland, a town on the Yellowstone), not one centre
redraw time (update, draw, flush) for the real grid tile at zooms 15, 16 and 17, with the CPU slowed 4 times to approximate a phone, and on one real phone if available
label count after the fit and collision tests per view, and the draw time of those labels with and without halo
V8 heap and typed-array bytes per feature for the shard layout; canvas bytes per layer
the canvas acceleration status of the target browsers (this VM: 2D canvas software only)
gate for the zoom thresholds: a visual check of the real tile at zooms 15, 16 and 17 on a 390 px and a 1280 px screen, light and dark

addresses_gzip_grid_tile.method: DBF streamed once; grid tile [45.7,45.8]x[-108.6,-108.5]; duplicates merged; no-street rows left out

contrast.note: street and footprint colours are proposals built from existing tokens (map.css lines 7-30, 100-115); the hazard stroke colours are the chip colours of each mode (map.css --hz-*, --chip-*).

open_questions: Owner decision: the B3 brief shows address dots from zoom 13. One Billings viewport at zoom 13 holds 65,057 addresses in 64 shards (4.18 MB raw). This record proposes zoom 15 for dots and a count layer at 13. Not decided here.

Footprint licence: the FEMA and ORNL file metadata states no constraints; the hosted item states CC BY 4.0; the footprints worker asks FEMA for written confirmation. The look test drew a 293-structure sample for the look only and published nothing. Counsel and FEMA still to answer.

USGS terms: the two USGS policy pages returned HTTP 403 to a scripted request in this run and were not bypassed. The public-domain quote comes from earlier research evidence (research/globe/validation-evidence/base-imagery.json). Re-check in a browser before the site names USGS as a source for streets or footprints.

USGS maximum detail: both services return HTTP 404 at zoom 17 (the metadata gives 1:9,028 as the maximum scale). The imagery base and any layer that relies on it stop at zoom 16 unless another source is used.

TIGER vintage and grid: this record uses TIGER/Line 2026 (D16) on the store grid tile r0092_c0214. The streets worker used TIGER 2025 on an off-grid tile (45.75 to 45.85 N, 108.55 to 108.45 W). Their figures reproduce within about 1 percent on the 2026 file; re-measure on the store grid in the build.

Device speed: every timing is one 4-vCPU VM with software 2D canvas. A phone will be slower and may behave differently. No CPU slowdown run was made and no phone was measured; both belong in the build measurements.
Zoom 17 on the real tile was not timed: the real-tile runs alternate zooms 15 and 16. The zoom 17 counts and bytes come from the file-based model, not from a draw test.

Per-path raw at twice the count has one run (4.0 s pan); the SVG control has one run and times only the synchronous update (paint is not included). The batched raw layer was measured at three runs at each count.

Footprint draw cost uses synthetic 8-vertex polygons; the real footprint geometry (293 structures) was used for the look test only. A real-geometry draw test on the full tile needs the footprint geometry for the tile (not downloaded here).
The rural sample (Benchland) was not measured for shard bytes in this record; the footprints worker recorded 28 footprints and 2 address points in its 0.01-degree box.

GitHub Pages limits: measured statewide shard files are 4,212 address shards and 5,143 footprint shards (byte cap), plus the street shards, which were not counted. Measured raw bytes are 135.8 MB for footprints and 43.1 MB for addresses; streets are the streets worker's estimate of about 69 MB of coordinates. At the observed gzip ratios the total would be roughly 50 MB on the wire, an estimate. The published Pages size and file-count limits were not checked in this run.
The street tile byte counts include names and classes in one array per shard; a name table would reduce repeated names. Not measured here.
Label widths were not stored per name; the fit test used the browser measureText result inside each run. A per-name width table would let the build precompute the fit test.
